title: a first run asks the operator only what it cannot find out, `fm doctor` says for every dependency and every vendor login whether it works here and how to fix it, and a crew round never runs on a login it did not check
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-26/27 the captain lost hours to things a doctor would have said up front: codex out of quota, found only when a canary round failed; gemini's OAuth expired; cursor unable to use `agent login` inside the sandbox; a stray `bin/__pycache__` making a worktree look dirty. Research on kunchenguid/firstmate (firstmate-ops/research/vendor-management.md §1 and §8) found three cheap practices worth taking: (1) before launching claude, shed the environment credentials that silently outrank the subscription login; (2) check a vendor's login with a fixed-argv, stdin-closed, time-bounded probe, where anything but a clear 'authenticated' fails; (3) dispatch by remaining quota (that is T-124, not this task). The captain approved this plan on 2026-09-27. This task absorbs the doctor part of T-078 without its plugin layout. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-121.json, is committed on this branch.

Toolchain. `mise.toml` pins every tool firstmate itself needs: bun, node, python, jq, gh, and anything bin/ci.sh or the board calls. `fm doctor` checks each against the pin and prints `ok` / `missing` / `wrong version` with the one command that fixes it (`mise install`, or the tool's own installer when mise can't). It installs nothing unless asked (`fm doctor --fix`, which asks before each install). Test with a PATH that lacks a tool and one with a wrong version.

Vendor logins, checked the same way everywhere. `bin/fm-auth-probe.sh <vendor>` runs the vendor's own status check (`claude auth status`, `codex login status`, `cursor-agent status`, gemini's equivalent, each taken from the vendor's docs or a recorded transcript). It uses a fixed argv, stdin closed, a scrubbed environment (HOME, PATH, TMPDIR, USER, LOGNAME, plus only what that vendor's login needs), and a time limit (about 20 s). It prints exactly one of `authenticated`, `unauthenticated`, `expired`, `quota-exhausted`, `indeterminate`, `timeout`, `unavailable` (not installed), followed by a one-line reason in en and zh-TW, and never echoes vendor output or a secret. Only `authenticated` counts as usable; `indeterminate` is never read as authenticated. It records the vendor version it probed. fm-worker.sh and fm-review.sh run it for the vendor before a round, and a round on anything but `authenticated` is refused with the probe's reason on the board, instead of failing inside the sandbox. Stubs answer exactly as each vendor's CLI does, from a recorded transcript.

Credentials that outrank the subscription are shed. The claude adapter launches claude with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` and any other variable claude documents as outranking the stored login, unset, unless the operator explicitly chose API-key billing in config.yaml. The one token fm hands in for the round (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, per T-117) is the only credential left. The same rule applies to the other vendors: each has a documented list of variables that change which account or billing is used, and anything the operator didn't choose is removed. `fm doctor` warns when such a variable is set in the operator's shell, because it would change billing for their own interactive use too. Test per vendor that the round's environment has exactly the credential the policy names.

Sandbox reality check. `fm doctor --sandbox` runs `bin/fm-canary.sh` for every installed vendor and summarises it: started, authenticated, every probe blocked, and whether a round's own loopback works on this host. It prints the fix for each failure: the one-time `security add-generic-password -s firstmate-cursor-api-key` step for cursor, 'start gemini once outside a round' for an expired gemini login, and the quota reset time when the vendor says so. firstmate's merge gate for sandbox-touching PRs uses this command.

First run. `fm setup` (and `fm doctor` when no settings exist) asks only what it cannot find out, each with a recommended default that Enter accepts: which installed vendors crew as worker and as reviewer (recommend a different vendor for review when two are usable); for each chosen vendor, the login method that works inside the sandbox and whether it bills to the subscription or per use (stated plainly); the main repository and base branch (after checking `gh auth status` and push rights); (the board port and language moved to T-154 by the captain, 2026-09-29). It writes config.yaml, then runs `fm doctor --sandbox`. It never asks for or stores a secret itself. For a key, it prints the exact keychain command for the operator to run. Test the wizard non-interactively with an answers file, and with all defaults.

Repository hygiene. `.gitignore` ignores `__pycache__/` if T-123 has not already done so, and `fm doctor` flags untracked build caches in state/worktrees that would make firstmate's sync skip a worktree.

Docs and board. README gets an install section: mise, `fm setup`, `fm doctor`. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md says firstmate runs `fm doctor` at startup and before dispatching to a vendor it has not probed this session. The board shows a vendor that is not `authenticated` as unavailable, with the probe's reason, en and zh-TW. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suite themselves.

Folded in from T-078 (removed 2026-09-28, captain approved): `fm doctor` checks every dependency firstmate needs (git, gh, bun, python3, jq, herdr, the OS sandbox tool, each vendor CLI) and, for each one missing or too old, says in one line how to install it on this OS. T-079 now depends on this task instead of T-078.
